title: Best WordPress Developers (2026): Hire One for Your Site
description: How to hire a WordPress developer: what to ask for, how to brief the job, what affects the price and the warning signs to watch for.
intro: WordPress runs a large share of the web because it is flexible and easy to edit once it is set up well. Set up badly, it becomes slow, hard to update and easy to hack. The difference usually comes down to the theme, the plugins and the handover, so this guide focuses on those.

faq.q: Will I be able to edit the site myself afterwards?
faq.a: You should be. Ask for a page builder or block editor you can use without code, and a short guide or screen recording showing how to change text, images and menus. Confirm this in the brief.

faq.q: Are premium themes and plugins included?
faq.a: Not always. Some developers use their own license, which may stop receiving updates once the order ends. Ask whether licenses are transferred to you or whether you should buy them in your own name.

faq.q: Can a WordPress developer fix or update my existing site?
faq.a: Yes, many gigs cover fixes, speed work and redesigns. Before they start, take a full backup and make sure it can be restored, and ask whether they will test changes on a copy of the site first.

faq.q: How many plugins is too many?
faq.a: There is no fixed number. What matters is that each plugin is needed, well maintained and up to date. Ask the developer to list every plugin they install and what it does.

faq.q: Who handles WordPress updates and backups after launch?
faq.a: Unless it is written into the order, you do. Core, theme and plugin updates are needed for security. Many developers offer maintenance as a separate service; ask what it covers.
